cases.title: K.W. v. Armstrong — pre-action stay, evidence access, and burden shift
cases.jurisdiction: United States - Idaho and Ninth Circuit
cases.problem: Individual Medicaid budgets were reduced through a budgeting process while notices failed to give participants a usable individualized basis for challenge.
cases.intervention: Class litigation and preliminary injunction preserved prior budgets, required adequate individualized notice, and required access to specified calculation records before reductions.
cases.observed_outcome: The status quo was preserved and prior budget levels restored while the acting institution was required to justify and disclose the basis before confirming reductions.
cases.durability_state: multi-year judicial supervision and appellate affirmance; later tooling and settlement compliance require continued review
costs_and_limits: the case did not create general co-governance over Medicaid objectives
the remedy is jurisdiction- and program-specific
cases.transferable_mechanism: Automatic or readily available pre-deprivation stay plus individualized notice, access to the operative calculation, independent review, and a burden on the acting institution.

cases.title: SyRI — collective challenge and system-level prohibition
cases.domain: social-welfare fraud analytics and cross-agency data use
cases.problem: A statutory risk-indication system combined data for fraud detection without sufficient transparency and verifiability.
cases.intervention: Civil-society claimants, private individuals and a trade union challenged the statutory framework; the Hague District Court found it incompatible with Article 8 ECHR and declared it without binding effect.
cases.observed_outcome: The legal basis could not continue to authorize SyRI in its existing form.
cases.durability_state: system-level legal prohibition is observed; deletion, individual remedy and successor-system recurrence remain acquisition objects
costs_and_limits: the public record does not establish compensation for every affected person
the ruling does not prove that no functionally similar successor can emerge
the mechanism depends on collective legal standing and an independent court
cases.transferable_mechanism: Collective standing, independent proportionality review, disclosure sufficient to test the system, and authority to disable the legal basis rather than merely correct one record.

cases.title: Homes for Ukraine Share — observed public-platform substitution
cases.domain: public digital service and sensitive case management
cases.problem: A time-critical national service relied on a supplier-owned platform for sensitive data sharing across central and local government.
cases.intervention: MHCLG built an in-house replacement, migrated three years of operational data, trained users, launched Share, exited the supplier contract, and continued the service.
cases.observed_outcome: A bounded public institution demonstrated practical substitution and regained ownership of system data and code while maintaining a live service.
cases.durability_state: continuing operation and releases are reported; independent long-run performance, residual custody and full deletion remain open
costs_and_limits: this is one bounded public service, not enterprise proof for every Palantir deployment
reported savings and usability gains are principally an official delivery account
guest co-governance over categories and purposes is not established
cases.transferable_mechanism: Internal multidisciplinary capacity, early migration planning, user research, phased quality assurance, training, public ownership of code and data, and post-transition operation.

cases.title: Robodebt Royal Commission — retrospective reconstruction and institutional learning
cases.problem: A large-scale automated administrative scheme generated debts and proof burdens whose operation later required extensive public reconstruction.
cases.intervention: A Royal Commission used compulsory information and document powers, public hearings, submissions and a final report with 57 recommendations.
cases.observed_outcome: The scheme and institutional conduct were reconstructed through an authoritative public record and recommendations, creating a basis for accountability and reform.
cases.durability_state: public reconstruction is durable; implementation, compensation, successor systems and private-benefit allocation require separate outcome tracking
costs_and_limits: the principal intervention was retrospective after extensive harm
a commission report is not itself complete compensation or co-governance
the source set does not close a private error-to-benefit chain
cases.transferable_mechanism: Compulsory evidence preservation, public testimony, versioned technical records, independent inquiry, public findings, and tracked implementation.

why_not: no case in the initial benchmark demonstrates R6 co-governance
no case demonstrates R7 value recovery as an institutional rule
the observed mechanisms are distributed across different systems rather than combined into one durable answer
direct affected-person power, costs, durability and successor-system regression remain incomplete in several cases
candidate_answer: access to the operative evidence, threshold and version
public capacity to substitute the system
enforceable co-governance over purpose and thresholds
recovery of value created through public authority, data, labor, risk or injury
